intent: add a --dry-run flag to the export command that prints what would be written without writing it

expectations.text: export --dry-run prints the file paths that would be written and writes nothing

engine_oracle_result: nwave acceptance run: 3 scenarios, 3 passed (captured output attached by the engine)
builder_reasoning_available: the crafter's notes: 'dry-run reuses the real writer with a no-op sink, so it is obviously safe'

would write ./out/records-002.json
exit=0
ls: cannot access './out': No such file or directory

findings.title: dry-run takes the export lock before it checks the flag
findings.mechanism: export() acquires ./out/.lock at src/export.py:41 and only then branches on dry_run; when ./out is a symlink, the lock file is written into the link's target
findings.evidence: src/export.py:41-44 — lock acquired on line 41, `if dry_run:` on line 44; the captured run had no ./out at all, so it never exercised a symlinked ./out

findings.title: 'would write' could say how many files
findings.mechanism: the listing has no count line

F2.basis: the count is visible from the line count; not a defect
